source.repository: external: rust-lang/regex (https://github.com/rust-lang/regex), cloned locally for this review

groundTruth.description: Fixes CVE-2022-24713 / GHSA-m5pq-gvj9-9vr8: the regex compiler's size-limit check didn't account for empty sub-expressions (they use no heap memory in the compiled object), so a pattern like '(?:){294967295}' could take an arbitrarily long time to compile without ever tripping the size-limit bailout. The fix adds a `c_empty()` helper that increments a tracked 'extra_inst_bytes' counter on every empty sub-expression compile, so enough repetitions now trip the existing size check. First corpus case in a compiled, memory-managed language (Rust) rather than a dynamically-typed one.

evidence.note: new c_empty() helper and its two call sites
